problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡3x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}?$

feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡2x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=\frac{5\pi }{12},\frac{11\pi }{12}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{12}+\frac{11\pi }{12}=\frac{4\pi }{3}.
$$
